messages.content: Now compare the three Back Bay hotels for April 14 through 17. I need the real three-night totals and a workable place to leave my bag after Saturday checkout.

Using the current quotes, the meeting hotel is $318 a night, the smaller hotel four blocks away is $286, and the station-area hotel is $279 plus a $35 nightly facility charge. I’ll put taxes and Saturday storage on the same basis before recommending one.
The tax shown is 16.45% for all three. Is the facility charge taxed too?
Yes, the station-area quote taxes both the room and facility charge. Its calculation is $837 room, $105 facility charge, and $154.96 tax, for $1,096.96 total.

The meeting hotel is $954 before tax, plus $156.93 tax, totaling $1,110.93. The smaller hotel is $858 before tax, plus $141.14 tax, totaling $999.14. The spread from lowest to highest is $111.79 for the full stay.
How do they compare for the appointments? Everything is at or beside the meeting hotel.

The meeting hotel is effectively a zero-to-two-minute walk. The smaller property is about seven minutes away, roughly four blocks. The station-area option is about an eleven-minute walk, though it is the easiest of the three for reaching Back Bay station.
Check the Saturday problem carefully. The panel may run until 12:40, and I need to retrieve the bag and leave around 1:05 for the 4:05 flight.

The meeting hotel confirms complimentary storage after checkout, with the bell desk staffed continuously that afternoon; retrieval should take only a few minutes. The station-area hotel also stores bags without charge and has a staffed desk all day. The smaller hotel accepts bags, but its reception desk closes at noon Saturday and retrieval after noon requires a separately arranged staff handoff. That is too uncertain for a 1:05 departure.

The meeting hotel allows cancellation without penalty through 6:00 p.m. local time on April 12. The smaller hotel requires cancellation by 3:00 p.m. on April 10. The station-area rate is cancelable through 6:00 p.m. on April 11. After those deadlines, each quote shows a one-night room-and-tax charge.
So the station hotel only saves about fourteen dollars compared with the meeting hotel once its fee is included?
Correct. The exact difference is $13.97. In exchange, it adds about nine minutes of walking each way to the meeting site. Its storage is workable, but it offers little meaningful savings.
Then keep the meeting hotel. Give me a reservation request the office can act on, but make clear what still needs confirmation.

Reserve the Copley Square Hotel for one room, checking in Wednesday, April 14 and checking out Saturday, April 17, for three nights. Use the quoted $318 nightly rate and confirm an all-in total of $1,110.93, including $156.93 tax and no facility charge. Request complimentary luggage storage after Saturday checkout, with immediate bell-desk retrieval around 12:40-12:50 p.m., so departure for Logan can occur by about 1:05 p.m. Before completing the reservation, verify the room type, exact property and meeting addresses, deposit or card authorization, check-in and checkout times, cancellation without penalty through 6:00 p.m. local time April 12, the post-deadline penalty, and that the bell desk will be staffed continuously Saturday afternoon. The flight plan remains the Wednesday nonstop arriving at 12:55 p.m. and the Saturday 4:05 p.m. nonstop, with the 6:10 p.m. return retained as the fallback if panel timing, bag retrieval, airline cutoff, traffic, or security conditions do not support the earlier departure.
